sentences.text: Rule thirty covers anchored and aground vessels.
A vessel at anchor shows an all-round white light in the fore part, and at or near the stern a second all-round white light, lower than the forward one.
A vessel under fifty meters may instead show one all-round white light where it can best be seen.
A vessel one hundred meters or more must also illuminate her decks with working lights.
A vessel aground shows her anchor lights plus two all-round red lights in a vertical line.
By day, one ball means at anchor, and three balls in a vertical line means aground.
